No state machines, lifecycle transitions or error-handling behavior are specified by these fragments.
Numeric note types from NT_ARM_ZA onward, including ZA, ZT, FPMR, POE, GCS, ARC_V2, VMCOREDD, MIPS, RISCV and LOONGARCH families, are not visible because the final fragment truncates after NN_ARM_ZA.

findings.text: Early machine codes use small decimal values. EM_NONE is 0, EM_M32 is 1, EM_SPARC is 2, EM_386 is 3, EM_68K is 4, EM_88K is 5, EM_486 is 6 noted as perhaps disused, EM_860 is 7, and EM_MIPS is 8 for big-endian R3000.

Middle machine codes continue the table. EM_MIPS_RS3_LE is 10 for little-endian R3000 and EM_MIPS_RS4_BE is also 10 for big-endian R4000, EM_PARISC is 15, EM_SPARC32PLUS is 18, EM_PPC is 20, EM_PPC64 is 21, EM_SPU is 23, EM_ARM is 40, EM_SH is 42, EM_SPARCV9 is 43, EM_H8_300 is 46, EM_IA_64 is 50, EM_X86_64 is 62, and EM_S390 is 22.

Later machine codes cover embedded, accelerator and modern architectures. EM_CRIS is 76, EM_M32R is 88, EM_MN10300 is 89, EM_OPENRISC is 92, EM_ARCOMPACT is 93, EM_XTENSA is 94, EM_BLACKFIN is 106, EM_UNICORE is 110, EM_ALTERA_NIOS2 is 113, EM_TI_C6000 is 140, EM_HEXAGON is 164, EM_NDS32 is 167, EM_AARCH64 is 183, EM_TILEPRO is 188, EM_MICROBLAZE is 189, EM_TILEGX is 191, EM_ARCV2 is 195, EM_RISCV is 243, EM_BPF is 247 for the in-kernel virtual machine, EM_CSKY is 252, EM_LOONGARCH is 258, and EM_FRV is 0x5441.
Legacy vendor machine codes use large hexadecimal values. EM_ALPHA is 0x9026, EM_CYGNUS_M32R is 0x9041, EM_S390_OLD is 0xA390, and EM_CYGNUS_MN10300 is 0xbeef.

The 32-bit FDPIC load description pairs segment and map types. Type elf32_fdpic_loadseg holds mapped address in addr and file address in p_vaddr, both using Elf32_Addr, plus allocation size in p_memsz using Elf32_Word. Type elf32_fdpic_loadmap holds revision in version and count in nsegs, both using Elf32_Half, plus trailing array segs. Constant ELF32_FDPIC_LOADMAP_VERSION is 0x0000.

The 64-bit FDPIC load description mirrors the 32-bit shape with wider addresses. Type elf64_fdpic_loadseg holds mapped address in addr and file address in p_vaddr, both using Elf64_Addr, plus size in p_memsz using Elf64_Word. Type elf64_fdpic_loadmap holds revision in version and count in nsegs, both using Elf64_Half, plus trailing array segs. Constant ELF64_FDPIC_LOADMAP_VERSION is 0x0000.

The GNU stack program header type is derived from the OS-specific base. Both the generic ELF header and the FDPIC header define PT_GNU_STACK as PT_LOOS plus 0x474e551, so consumers in either header see the same numeric type.

32-bit ELF scalar aliases fix widths and signedness. Elf32_Addr, Elf32_Off and Elf32_Word build on 32-bit unsigned base, Elf32_Half and Elf32_Versym on 16-bit unsigned base, and Elf32_Sword on 32-bit signed base.

64-bit ELF scalar aliases fix wider address and offset types. Elf64_Addr and Elf64_Off use 64-bit unsigned base, Elf64_Word uses 32-bit unsigned, Elf64_Xword uses 64-bit unsigned and Elf64_Sxword uses 64-bit signed, Elf64_Half and Elf64_Versym use 16-bit unsigned with Elf64_SHalf as signed 16-bit, and Elf64_Sword uses 32-bit signed.

Program header types identify segment roles and reserved ranges. PT_NULL is 0, PT_LOAD is 1, PT_DYNAMIC is 2, PT_INTERP is 3, PT_NOTE is 4, PT_SHLIB is 5, PT_PHDR is 6, and PT_TLS is 7. PT_LOOS to PT_HIOS span 0x60000000 to 0x6fffffff while PT_LOPROC to PT_HIPROC span 0x70000000 to 0x7fffffff. PT_GNU_EH_FRAME, PT_GNU_STACK, PT_GNU_RELRO and PT_GNU_PROPERTY are the OS base plus 0x474e550 through 0x474e553 respectively, and PT_AARCH64_MEMTAG_MTE is the processor base plus 2.

File types and the section-count overflow sentinel are fixed. ET_NONE is 0, ET_REL is 1, ET_EXEC is 2, ET_DYN is 3, and ET_CORE is 4, with ET_LOPROC to ET_HIPROC spanning 0xff00 to 0xffff. PN_XNUM is 0xffff and signals that the real section count lives elsewhere.

Low dynamic tags use small decimal values. DT_NULL is 0, DT_NEEDED is 1, DT_PLTRELSZ is 2, DT_PLTGOT is 3, DT_HASH is 4, DT_STRTAB is 5, DT_SYMTAB is 6, DT_RELA is 7, DT_RELASZ is 8, DT_RELAENT is 9, DT_STRSZ is 10, DT_SYMENT is 11, DT_INIT is 12, DT_FINI is 13, DT_SONAME is 14, DT_RPATH is 15, DT_SYMBOLIC is 16, DT_REL is 17, DT_RELSZ is 18, DT_RELENT is 19, DT_PLTREL is 20, DT_DEBUG is 21, DT_TEXTREL is 22, DT_JMPREL is 23, and DT_ENCODING is 32.

High dynamic tags use OS, value, address and processor ranges. OLD_DT_LOOS is 0x60000000, DT_LOOS is 0x6000000d and DT_HIOS is 0x6ffff000. DT_VALRNGLO to DT_VALRNGHI span 0x6ffffd00 to 0x6ffffdff and DT_ADDRRNGLO to DT_ADDRRNGHI span 0x6ffffe00 to 0x6ffffeff, with DT_GNU_HASH at 0x6ffffef5. Further fixed tags are DT_VERSYM at 0x6ffffff0, DT_RELACOUNT at 0x6ffffff9, DT_RELCOUNT at 0x6ffffffa, DT_FLAGS_1 at 0x6ffffffb, DT_VERDEF at 0x6ffffffc, DT_VERDEFNUM at 0x6ffffffd, DT_VERNEED at 0x6ffffffe and DT_VERNEEDNUM at 0x6fffffff. OLD_DT_HIOS is 0x6fffffff and DT_LOPROC to DT_HIPROC span 0x70000000 to 0x7fffffff.

Symbol binding, type and version flags use small values. STB_LOCAL is 0, STB_GLOBAL is 1 and STB_WEAK is 2, with STN_UNDEF at 0. STT_NOTYPE is 0, STT_OBJECT is 1, STT_FUNC is 2, STT_SECTION is 3, STT_FILE is 4, STT_COMMON is 5 and STT_TLS is 6. VER_FLG_BASE is 1 and VER_FLG_WEAK is 2.

Symbol info packs binding above type in one byte. ELF_ST_BIND recovers binding by shifting right four, while ELF_ST_TYPE recovers type by masking low four. ELF32_ST_BIND with ELF32_ST_TYPE and ELF64_ST_BIND with ELF64_ST_TYPE alias the generic pair for each class.

Dynamic entry types pair tag with union. Elf32_Dyn carries tag in d_tag as signed 32-bit and payload in d_un choosing between d_val as signed value or d_ptr as address. Elf64_Dyn carries tag in d_tag as signed 64-bit and payload in d_un choosing between d_val as unsigned extended value or d_ptr as address.

Relocation info packs index above type. ELF32_R_SYM shifts right eight for index while ELF32_R_TYPE masks low eight for type. ELF64_R_SYM shifts right thirty-two for index while ELF64_R_TYPE masks low thirty-two for type.

Relocation types locate action plus target. Types elf32_rel and Elf32_Rel carry offset in r_offset and index-plus-type in r_info with narrow widths, while elf64_rel and Elf64_Rel use wide address and extended info. Addend forms elf32_rela with Elf32_Rela and elf64_rela with Elf64_Rela add signed addend in r_addend to the same offset and info pair.

Symbol types differ in order. Type elf32_sym with Elf32_Sym orders name in st_name, value in st_value, size in st_size, binding-plus-type in st_info, visibility in st_other and section in st_shndx. Type elf64_sym with Elf64_Sym orders st_name, then st_info, st_other and st_shndx, followed by st_value and st_size.

File header types share logical sequence. Types elf32_hdr with Elf32_Ehdr and elf64_hdr with Elf64_Ehdr start with identifier array e_ident sized by EI_NIDENT at 16, then type in e_type, machine in e_machine, version in e_version, entry in e_entry, program offset in e_phoff, section offset in e_shoff, flags in e_flags, header size in e_ehsize, program entry size and count in e_phentsize with e_phnum, section entry size and count in e_shentsize with e_shnum, and string index in e_shstrndx.
Segment permission flags are single bits. PF_R is 4, PF_W is 2 and PF_X is 1, combinable to describe readable, writable and executable mappings.

Program header types differ in order. Type elf32_phdr with Elf32_Phdr orders kind in p_type, file position in p_offset, virtual address in p_vaddr, physical address in p_paddr, file size in p_filesz, memory size in p_memsz, flags in p_flags and alignment in p_align. Type elf64_phdr with Elf64_Phdr places p_type with p_flags first, then p_offset, p_vaddr, p_paddr, p_filesz, p_memsz and p_align.

Section types use small values plus reserved ranges. SHT_NULL is 0, SHT_PROGBITS is 1, SHT_SYMTAB is 2, SHT_STRTAB is 3, SHT_RELA is 4, SHT_HASH is 5, SHT_DYNAMIC is 6, SHT_NOTE is 7, SHT_NOBITS is 8, SHT_REL is 9, SHT_SHLIB is 10, SHT_DYNSYM is 11 and SHT_NUM is 12. SHT_LOPROC to SHT_HIPROC span 0x70000000 to 0x7fffffff and SHT_LOUSER to SHT_HIUSER span 0x80000000 to 0xffffffff.

Section flags are bit masks. SHF_WRITE is 1, SHF_ALLOC is 2, SHF_EXECINSTR is 4, SHF_MERGE is 16, SHF_STRINGS is 32, SHF_INFO_LINK is 64, SHF_LINK_ORDER is 128, SHF_OS_NONCONFORMING is 256, SHF_GROUP is 512, SHF_TLS is 1024, SHF_RELA_LIVEPATCH is 0x100000, SHF_RO_AFTER_INIT is 0x200000, SHF_ORDERED is 0x4000000 and SHF_EXCLUDE is 0x8000000. SHF_MASKOS is 0x0ff00000 and SHF_MASKPROC is 0xf0000000.

Special section indices reserve high values. SHN_UNDEF is 0, SHN_LORESERVE and SHN_LOPROC are both 0xff00, SHN_HIPROC is 0xff1f, SHN_LIVEPATCH is 0xff20, SHN_ABS is 0xfff1, SHN_COMMON is 0xfff2 and SHN_HIRESERVE is 0xffff.

Section header types share ten-field logic. Types elf32_shdr with Elf32_Shdr and elf64_shdr with Elf64_Shdr carry name in sh_name, kind in sh_type, attributes in sh_flags, address in sh_addr, file position in sh_offset, length in sh_size, association in sh_link, extra info in sh_info, alignment in sh_addralign and table step in sh_entsize, with wider flags and sizes in 64-bit.

Identification bytes and file metadata use fixed positions and values. EI_MAG0 through EI_MAG3 are 0 to 3, EI_CLASS is 4, EI_DATA is 5, EI_VERSION is 6, EI_OSABI is 7 and EI_PAD is 8. ELFMAG0 is 127 with ELFMAG1 through ELFMAG3 matching letters E L F, SELFMAG is 4 and ELFMAG joins the octal escape for 127 to ELF. ELFCLASSNONE is 0, ELFCLASS32 is 1, ELFCLASS64 is 2 and ELFCLASSNUM is 3. ELFDATANONE is 0, ELFDATA2LSB is 1 and ELFDATA2MSB is 2. EV_NONE is 0, EV_CURRENT is 1 and EV_NUM is 2. ELFOSABI_NONE is 0 and ELFOSABI_LINUX is 3, with ELF_OSABI selecting none.
The GNU property note pairs NN_GNU_PROPERTY_TYPE_0 holding GNU with NT_GNU_PROPERTY_TYPE_0 at 5, distinguishing property notes from core and Linux notes.

Low core notes share owner CORE. NT_PRSTATUS is 1 with NN_PRSTATUS, NT_PRFPREG is 2 with NN_PRFPREG, NT_PRPSINFO is 3 with NN_PRPSINFO, NT_TASKSTRUCT is 4 with NN_TASKSTRUCT and NT_AUXV is 6 with NN_AUXV.

Extended notes mix mnemonic and sequential types. NT_SIGINFO with NN_SIGINFO is 0x53494749 and NT_FILE with NN_FILE is 0x46494c45 under CORE, while NT_PRXFPREG with NN_PRXFPREG is 0x46e62b7f under LINUX. PowerPC LINUX notes increment by one from NT_PPC_VMX at 256, NT_PPC_SPE at 257, NT_PPC_VSX at 258, NT_PPC_TAR at 259, NT_PPC_PPR at 260, NT_PPC_DSCR at 261, NT_PPC_EBB at 262, NT_PPC_PMU at 263, NT_PPC_TM_CGPR at 264, NT_PPC_TM_CFPR at 265, NT_PPC_TM_CVMX at 266, NT_PPC_TM_CVSX at 267, NT_PPC_TM_SPR at 268, NT_PPC_TM_CTAR at 269, NT_PPC_TM_CPPR at 270, NT_PPC_TM_CDSCR at 271, NT_PPC_PKEY at 272, NT_PPC_DEXCR at 273 and NT_PPC_HASHKEYR at 274, each with matching NN_PPC name holding LINUX.

x86 LINUX notes use types 512 through 517 with one gap. NT_386_TLS with NN_386_TLS is 512, NT_386_IOPERM with NN_386_IOPERM is 513, NT_X86_XSTATE with NN_X86_XSTATE is 514, NT_X86_SHSTK with NN_X86_SHSTK is 516 and NT_X86_XSAVE_LAYOUT with NN_X86_XSAVE_LAYOUT is 517. Type 515 has no definition in the visible fragments.

s390 LINUX notes increment by one from 768 to 782. NT_S390_HIGH_GPRS is 768, NT_S390_TIMER is 769, NT_S390_TODCMP is 770, NT_S390_TODPREG is 771, NT_S390_CTRS is 772, NT_S390_PREFIX is 773, NT_S390_LAST_BREAK is 774, NT_S390_SYSTEM_CALL is 775, NT_S390_TDB is 776, NT_S390_VXRS_LOW is 777, NT_S390_VXRS_HIGH is 778, NT_S390_GS_CB is 779, NT_S390_GS_BC is 780, NT_S390_RI_CB is 781 and NT_S390_PV_CPU_DATA is 782, each with matching NN_S390 name holding LINUX.

ARM LINUX notes increment by one from 1024 to 1035 in the visible range. NT_ARM_VFP is 1024, NT_ARM_TLS is 1025, NT_ARM_HW_BREAK is 1026, NT_ARM_HW_WATCH is 1027, NT_ARM_SYSTEM_CALL is 1028, NT_ARM_SVE is 1029, NT_ARM_PAC_MASK is 1030, NT_ARM_PACA_KEYS is 1031, NT_ARM_PACG_KEYS is 1032, NT_ARM_TAGGED_ADDR_CTRL is 1033, NT_ARM_PAC_ENABLED_KEYS is 1034 and NT_ARM_SSVE is 1035, each with matching NN_ARM name holding LINUX. NN_ARM_ZA holding LINUX is visible without its numeric type in the truncated fragment.

Each header uses a conventional include guard. Macros _LINUX_ELF_EM_H, _UAPI_LINUX_ELF_FDPIC_H and _UAPI_LINUX_ELF_H are defined on first inclusion to prevent repeated definitions when the same UAPI header is pulled in multiple times.
Two MIPS machine names share the same numeric code 10, one labelled little-endian R3000 and the other big-endian R4000, so decoding the number alone cannot recover endianness or CPU revision.

Several 32-bit and 64-bit structures reorder or widen fields rather than appending, notably elf32_sym against elf64_sym and elf32_phdr against elf64_phdr, so casting or copying between classes without field-wise conversion corrupts addresses, sizes and flags.
FDPIC load-map versions for both widths are defined as zero, indicating the initial revision that readers must accept and writers must emit until a new version is specified.
